prompt: What was the latest recorded MRR change of each subscription of an account in Germany (country_code DE)? A subscription belongs to the country_code of its account. recorded_at is Brussels local time. Keep exactly one change per subscription, the one with the latest recorded_at. When two changes of a subscription tie on recorded_at, the lower event_id is kept. Return four columns, in this order: subscription_id, event_type, mrr_delta_local and recorded_at, from that change. Return one row for each such subscription. Any row order is fine.
hints: Next, write the outer query: it reads the numbered changes and keeps number 1 of each subscription.
The number exists only after the CTE has run, so the keep-one filter goes in the outer query's WHERE.
faded_shape:
WITH ranked AS (  -- one row per MRR change of a subscription of a German account
  SELECT e.subscription_id, e.event_type, e.mrr_delta_local, e.recorded_at,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY e.subscription_id ORDER BY e.recorded_at DESC, e.event_id) AS rn
  FROM subscription_events e
  JOIN accounts a ON a.account_id = e.account_id
  WHERE a.country_code = 'DE'
)
why_this_works: The outer filter keeps each subscription's change numbered 1, the latest recorded first with event_id settling a tie.
